text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- ABN Amro bank starts development of its own European payments and settlement system. (p1)
- U.S. IT consultancy bureau Perot Systems takes over Houten-based high-tech firm Syllogic. (p1)
- Number of people in paid employment with a second job sharply up last year. (p1)
- Transport minister opposes MPs' plan to curb Libertel and PTT Telecom's mobile phone network expansion for three years. (p3)
- Cabinet has doubts over Rotterdam's proposed Maasvlakte II port exrension and industrial park. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Dutch EU presidency will have initiated little change in Europe, it appears from final draft of the Amsterdam Treaty to be decided on during next week's summit. (p1)
- Dutch railways cuts 500 jobs in its maintenance unit. (p2)
- Bourse watchdog STE seeks to make companies' share option schemes subject to rules against insider trading. (p15)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Amsterdam police alerted after posters appear in city calling for assaults on European leaders during summit.
- Dutch cattle sector set for deep crisis. (p25)
- Philips chief J. Hommen still sees areas for substanial economising. (p27)
TROUW
- Amsterdam mayor Schelto Patijn does not expect riots during or around the European summit in Amsterdam. (p1)
- Brewer Grolsch hopes for warm weather and looks for new CEO to replace retiring Paul Snoep. (p7) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Payment and conditions accord reached between unions and Dutch PTT KPN. (p13)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
